text:
dmitri: quick favor — can someone run an isolated SKU sweep for a worst-case long-ctx p99 noise check? seeing weird spikes on prod traces that look hardware-dependent. want A100 / H100 / L40S comparison, same driver, same model, long seq (>=4096), kv_cache off vs on, batch sizes 1/4/8. no fancy autoscaling, single pinned process per GPU.
maya: yep i can take this if infra is free tonight. which model variant + quant do you want? fp16 or q4? also do you want nvlink enabled tests?
dmitri: start with fp16 (default) and q4hf, nvlink both enabled/disabled where possible — i suspect nvlink affects cache warmups for multi-gpu fanout. prioritize single-gpu as baseline. nvlink only for cases where model is sharded across >1 GPU.
racey: infra-bot: reserving three nodes for @maya tonight: a100-40gb-1, h100-80gb-2, l40s-48gb-3. driver pinned to 535.86. will drop if conflicts. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: reservation confirmed for 3h window starting 2051242000 — driver 535.86, kernel 5.15. If you need longer ping @eng-infra.
rick: quick note — disable preemption and set NUMA interleave off. we had a case where the scheduler moved threads and that created microbursts.
maya: copying the minimal command i'll run so folks can review. will upload raw perf traces + nvprof + dmesg. plan to run 3 repeats per config.

```bash
./bench/run_inference_sweep.sh \
  --model redwood/gpt-13b \
  --hw a100,h100,l40s \
  --seq 4096 \
  --batches 1,4,8 \
  --kv-cache false,true \
  --quant fp16,q4hf \
  --repeats 3 \
  --pin-cpu true \
  --collect nvprof,dmesg,trace
```

carla: couple asks — tag the run with git SHA (so we know kernel+runtime match) and include the kernel callgraph for the p99 samples (perf script folded). also collect SYSTEMD journal for the period.
dmitri: yep will create a PR to add the bench harness tag. expectation: produce CSV with p50/p90/p95/p99 and a small histogram per run plus raw tail traces. if you see consistent p99 > 2x between SKUs flag here and we'll schedule deep dive.
maya: started first pass on A100 now. small update: with kv_cache off p99s are noisy but median stable. uploading logs to https://git.redwood/internal/bench/runs/2051234567_a100_fp16_kvoff

rick: thanks. if A100 shows high variance while H100 low then check thermal throttling counters and sm_efficiency. on L40S watch nvlink fallback paths — we had a driver change that regressed fallback handling.
maya: noted. i'll put all driver counters + nvlink status in the artifacts. ETA for full sweep ~ 2.5 hrs. ping me if you want intermediate numbers.
dmitri: perfect. @carla once maya uploads, can you eyeball the p99 sample traces and call out top 3 syscall/wait reasons? your quick analysis helps prioritize whether it's scheduler/drivers/model-level.
carla: will do — plan: quick grep for stall reasons, then a short writeup with recommended next steps. :mag:
racey: left a small patch on the bench harness to normalize warmup sequences (PR: https://git.redwood/pr/bench/warmup-normalize). merging if no objections before maya runs next batch to keep runs comparable.
maya: acknowledged — i pulled that patch and will re-run warmup on the remaining configs.
dmitri: thanks all — let's regroup in thread with result CSVs. if anyone sees a clear SKU regression (eg A100 p99 > H100 p99 by >30%) call it out and we can open a kernel/driver triage immediately.
course-of-action: collect artifacts, produce CSV + histograms, carla does quick triage, then decide deep-dive owners. :chain:
_reserved_for_schema_note: Document represents a single Slack thread. messages are a single continuous string prefixed by sender names. No title field included.
